name: navier-stokes
title: Navier-Stokes: lid-driven cavity flow (IPCS)
question:
Does a real dolfinx incompressible Navier-Stokes solve -- Taylor-Hood-ish
P2/P1 velocity/pressure, classic IPCS (Incremental Pressure Correction
Scheme) operator splitting -- reproduce the textbook lid-driven-cavity
flow (a non-trivial, approximately divergence-free, quasi-steady
recirculating flow pinned near the lid velocity) when wrapped as a
process-bigraph Process, and does the scheme stay numerically stable
across a moderate Reynolds-number sweep?
hypothesis:
`NavierStokesProcess` should converge, within a fraction of a second of
simulated time, to a quasi-steady cavity flow whose peak speed sits near
the prescribed lid velocity (the moving-lid Dirichlet BC pins it there)
and whose velocity field is approximately divergence-free (small, not
exactly zero -- IPCS is only an approximate projection). The same IPCS
scheme, unmodified, should remain stable (no blow-up) from Re=100 up
through Re=1000 at this mesh/timestep, since diffusion is treated
implicitly (Crank-Nicolson) even though convection is explicit.
objective:
Run the `navier_stokes` composite (lid-driven cavity on the unit square,
P2 velocity / P1 pressure, IPCS splitting) to quasi-steady state and
verify (a) the flow is non-trivial and bounded near the lid velocity, (b)
the velocity field is approximately divergence-free, and (c) the same
scheme stays stable (finite, non-blown-up) across a Reynolds sweep
(100, 400, 1000).
description:
Wraps a single `NavierStokesProcess` in the `navier_stokes` composite
generator. Each tick, the process advances the lid-driven cavity flow by
`dt`-sized IPCS substeps: (1) a tentative-velocity solve (Crank-Nicolson
diffusion, explicit convection via the previous step's velocity), (2) a
pressure-correction Poisson solve using the tentative velocity's
divergence as a source, (3) a velocity-correction solve using the
pressure correction's gradient. All three are real
`dolfinx.fem.petsc.LinearProblem` direct solves -- no reimplementation of
the physics, no mock. `velocity_x`/`velocity_y`/`pressure`/
`speed_integral` are `overwrite` sensor outputs (the process's own
internally-persisted absolute flow state, freshly reported each tick),
mirroring `DiffusionProcess.integral`'s convention.

This is an ADVANCED, showcase-tier study within the investigation: it is
the first fluid-dynamics (as opposed to scalar diffusion/reaction) demo,
and the first to couple two different function spaces (P2 velocity, P1
pressure) in one process.

expected_behavior.name: reaches-quasi-steady
expected_behavior.en: speed_integral changes by less than 5% between two checkpoints late in the baseline run.
expected_behavior.condition: relative change in speed_integral between the last two checkpoints < 5%
expected_behavior.rationale: A well-posed lid-driven cavity solve should settle into a quasi-steady recirculating flow within a fraction of a second of simulated time, not oscillate or drift indefinitely; a small residual change between late checkpoints confirms convergence.

expected_behavior.name: approximately-divergence-free
expected_behavior.en: The mean absolute divergence of the converged velocity field is below 0.05 (resolution=24, Re=100).
expected_behavior.rationale: IPCS is an approximate projection method -- exact zero divergence is not expected -- but the mean absolute divergence over the domain should be small relative to the O(1) velocity scale and shrink under mesh refinement (observed ~0.003-0.02 at resolution=24 across Re=100..1000 during development), not blow up.

expected_behavior.name: stable-across-reynolds-sweep
expected_behavior.en: Every variant in the reynolds=[100,400,1000] sweep finishes with a finite max speed below 2x the lid velocity (no blow-up).
expected_behavior.condition: max(max_speed over sweep) < 2 * lid_velocity, all finite
expected_behavior.rationale: Non-stabilized (no SUPG) Galerkin FEM Navier-Stokes can develop grid-scale oscillations/blow-up at higher Reynolds number on a coarse mesh; this scheme's implicit (Crank-Nicolson) treatment of diffusion was verified during development to stay stable out to Re=1000 at this resolution/timestep (no reduction to a lower top Reynolds number was needed), and this test locks that finding.

behavior_tests.name: reaches-quasi-steady
behavior_tests.description:
The relative change in speed_integral between the checkpoint at
t=0.5 and a further checkpoint at t=0.6 must be below 5%.

provenance.note: 5% is a generous convergence band above the observed residual change (~1e-3 or smaller) once the cavity flow has settled, calibrated during development at resolution=24, dt=0.01.

behavior_tests.name: approximately-divergence-free
behavior_tests.description:
mean(|div(u)|) over the domain, computed via DG0 interpolation of
div(u_n), must be below 0.05 at the baseline (resolution=24, Re=100).

provenance.note: IPCS operator splitting introduces an O(dt) divergence residual (plus a local O(h) artifact at the lid's two discontinuous-BC corners) that is not exactly zero but should be small and shrink under refinement; 0.05 is well above the ~0.003 observed at this resolution during development.

behavior_tests.name: stable-across-reynolds-sweep
behavior_tests.description:
Across the reynolds=[100,400,1000] sweep, every variant's final max
speed must be finite and below 2x the lid velocity (no blow-up).

provenance.note: The lid BC directly prescribes the max speed at u=lid_velocity; 2x leaves generous headroom for transient overshoot while still catching a genuinely unstable/blown-up solve. Verified stable (no reduction from the planned Re=1000 top variant was needed) during development.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
No further studies in this investigation currently depend on
navier-stokes; it stands as the investigation's fluid-dynamics
showcase, built directly on the validated dolfinx bridge
(poisson-validation) rather than on the scalar diffusion/reaction
studies.
